description: MFA program checks mapped to NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 controls.

rules.title: Administrator without MFA
rules.remediation: Enroll the administrator in phishing-resistant MFA now and block privileged sign-in until it is in place.

rules.title: User without MFA
rules.remediation: Enroll the user in MFA and require registration at next sign-in.

rules.title: User still not enrolled after several monthly checks
rules.remediation: Contact the user and their manager directly; persistent non-enrollment usually means a missing phone, shared device, or unclear instructions.

rules.title: MFA removed or weakened since the previous snapshot
rules.remediation: Confirm the change was authorized. Unexpected removal or downgrade of MFA can indicate account takeover or a help desk process gap.

rules.title: Administrator without phishing-resistant MFA
rules.remediation: Issue FIDO2 security keys or certificate-based authentication to administrators and retire their phishable methods.

rules.title: User relies on SMS or voice MFA
rules.remediation: Move the user to an authenticator app or a phishing-resistant method; SMS and voice codes can be intercepted or redirected.

rules.title: Successful sign-ins through legacy protocols that bypass MFA
rules.remediation: Block legacy authentication protocols (such as IMAP, POP3, and basic-auth SMTP) and move the affected users and devices to modern authentication.

rules.title: Successful single-factor sign-ins through modern clients
rules.remediation: Extend MFA policies to cover these applications; single-factor modern sign-ins usually mean a policy exclusion or gap.

rules.title: MFA coverage target not on track
rules.remediation: Increase the enrollment pace or revise the target date; at the current rate the target will be missed.

rules.title: Administrator phishing-resistant MFA target not on track
rules.remediation: Prioritize security keys for administrators; this target is small in count and fast to close.
